{{Short description|Infinite mathematical manifold}}
[[File:Jacob s ladder surface.png|thumb|right]]
In mathematics,  '''Jacob's ladder''' is a [[two-dimensional manifold|surface]] with infinite [[Genus (mathematics)|genus]] and two [[End (topology)|ends]]. It was  named after [[Jacob's ladder]] by [[Étienne Ghys]],<ref>{{harvtxt|Ghys|1995|loc=Théorème A}}</ref> because the surface can be constructed as the boundary of a ladder that is infinitely long in both directions.
